context:
Goal: one red test drops only the lanes that broke it, so the rest of the batch merges green.
Problem (risk): many lanes touch test_merge.py, so a split that drops by touched file can drop most of a batch on one red.
Based on (read): the lane's round-1 findings on the split work (archive/merge-batch-split-and-pipeline-2, head ee4da8508).
Departs from: main has no batch split — adds one that drops lanes by touched file, or by a per-job hit map.
home: step two-drop-leaves-queue (a drop leaves the rest of the queue)

lastAnswer.note: Settled by a past ruling, not asked: decision batch-freeze-lane-set (owner Nov 8, 20:24 and 20:31 CST) says a red run drops the one lane that blame names, and its dependents. A drop by shared file departs from it; the split maps each red to the blamed lane.

options.gain: One red drops only the lanes that caused it.
options.how: The split maps each failing job to the lanes whose changes it ran, and drops only those.
options.label: Build the per-job hit map first (Recommended)
options.lose: More work before the split ships.

options.how: The split drops by touched file now; the hit map follows as a debt.
options.label: Ship the file split, hit map as a debt
options.lose: One red in test_merge.py can drop most of a batch.

ref: lane merge-batch-split-and-pipeline, via coordinator 14:07 CST Nov 12
reply: Closed 14:10 CST by triage: the past ruling settles it; the lane builds the per-job map.
short: Batch split: map reds to lanes
title: A red batch split drops lanes by shared file, or by the failing job
why: The split changes what the merge tool drops; that is your call.
